job.title: Assistant Site Manager - Tamworth
job.description:
About RWM
Regional Workforce Management (RWM) is proudly Australian-owned, dedicated to connecting businesses with tailored recruitment and workforce management solutions since 2000. Formerly FIP Group, we’ve spent over two decades supporting the backbone of Australia - the food, agriculture, forestry and fisheries industries. By blending local expertise with a national reach, we deliver reliable and committed people who help businesses grow, thrive and stand strong.

What started as a small operation helping local businesses quickly grew into something much bigger. Our founders’ ability to connect with people - sharing experiences, solutions and hope – helped forge strong bonds with businesses and communities alike. As we expanded from labour hire to permanent recruitment and into connecting skilled workers from across the borders, our mission has remained the same: to provide real solutions that save Australia’s food and agriculture business time and resources.

About The Role
We are currently seeking an Assistant Site Manager to support day-to-day operations and personnel onsite in Tamworth. This role will see you play a crucial role in fostering positive relationships and empowering staff.

This role is a permanent, full-time role (Monday-Friday).

In this position, your duties will also include:

  • Transportation of employees to clinics and appointments.

  • Manage accommodation and vehicle inspections and reports if required.
  • Support onsite employee wellbeing including regular check-ins and follow ups.
  • Assist with the education and mentoring of onsite employees in relation to workplace operations.
  • Fostering the relationship between the client and RWM onsite employees.
  • Conduct return to work procedures for site activities.
  • Escalate serious breaches or seek guidance on desired outcome to Internal HR.
  • Educate and coach onsite employees and visitors on safe site practices.
  • Monitor and report site safety and WHS policies and procedures.
  • Provide coverage or support to Site Managers in peak periods or to cover absences.

About You
To excel in this position, you should be committed to delivering results and supporting onsite personnel. Your dedication to this role and the fostering of positive relationships is crucial to your success in this role.

You should also possess the following attributes:

  • People management experience
  • Intermediate computer literacy, including Microsoft Suite skills

  • Exposure to the fundamentals of Human Resources, HR experience is desirable
  • Open Drivers Licence and reliable vehicle
  • Ability and willingness to receive a QFever vaccination and complete a Police Check

job.title: Livestock Technician
job.description:
About the Role
We are seeking a Livestock Technician who is responsible for providing technical, welfare, and operational support to contract and
company-owned duck broiler farms. The role focuses on optimising bird performance, animal welfare, biosecurity, and farm compliance while ensuring production targets are met in line with company standards and Australian
regulatory requirements.

This position is hands-on and field-based, requiring regular farm visits, data analysis, and close collaboration with
growers, hatchery, feed mill, and processing teams.

  • Full-time |38 hrs a weel
  • Pay rate: $70,000-$80,000
  • Located in Nhill VIC 3418


Key Responsibilities
Farm Management & Technical Support

  • Conduct regular farm visits to monitor flock health, growth, uniformity, livability and behaviour
  • Provide technical advice and practical support to growers on brooding, ventilation, stocking density, lighting, litter management and water quality
  • Monitor flock performance against key production targets, including FCR, ADG, mortality, condemnation rates and processing age, identifying opportunities for improvement

Animal Welfare, Biosecurity & Compliance

  • Ensure farms operate in accordance with company animal welfare standards, Australian poultry welfare guidelines, biosecurity requirements and relevant WHS and environmental legislation
  • Monitor farm practices, records and documentation, including mortality, medication, vaccinations, feed, water and maintenance
  • Identify and escalate disease, welfare, safety and compliance concerns, supporting investigations, audits and corrective actions
  • Promote humane bird handling, catching and depopulation practices, and ensure applicable Chain of Responsibility (CoR) and Heavy Vehicle National Law obligations are met

Performance Monitoring & Continuous Improvement

  • Collect, analyse and report on flock performance and production data, identifying trends and opportunities to improve productivity and operational outcomes
  • Complete farm service reports and contribute to flock reviews and production meetings
  • Support investigations into production issues, mortality, disease outbreaks and welfare concerns, as well as trials, new equipment and process improvements

Grower & Stakeholder Relationships

  • Build and maintain strong, professional relationships with growers, providing ongoing technical guidance, training and coaching
  • Work collaboratively with internal departments, including hatchery, feed mill, live haul, processing, Quality Assurance and veterinary teams, to resolve issues and achieve production objectives
  • Promote a culture of accountability, safety, animal welfare and continuous improvement across broiler operations

Additional Information and required experience:

  • Experience in poultry or livestock production, with duck experience highly regarded
  • A sound understanding of broiler production systems and flock management
  • Knowledge of animal welfare, biosecurity and farm safety practices
  • Strong observation, analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building abilities
  • The ability to work independently, manage priorities and make sound decisions in a field-based environment
  • Competent computer skills, including Microsoft Excel and production reporting systems
  • A current driver's licence
  • A qualification in Agriculture, Animal Science or a related discipline highly regarded
  • Familiarity with Australian poultry welfare standards and Chain of Responsibility obligations
